concepts.title: Assessment Information
concepts.authored_definition: A managed information artifact documenting an assessment and its scope, basis, methods, time context, participants and results. It is distinct from performing that assessment.
concepts.rationale: Retain the NIST security-report comparison as a documentary precedent. It describes an output of assessment, not the assessment activity or a universal enterprise/ecosystem report template.
concepts.context_interpretation: R-11 targets the continuing RiskCase; R-12 records basis and R-13/R-17 allow dimensional and score outputs. RX-014 pins context version, while optional method links are completed under the selected analytical task. Revised RiskCase and ArtifactVersion neighbors were reviewed.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Assessment Basis
concepts.authored_definition: A specification of assumptions and control conditions under which an assessment result is interpreted.
concepts.rationale: Clarify the former scoped-absence label as a contrast in definitional scope: generic prov:Entity can describe provenance, but does not define risk-specific assumptions or control conditions. No disjointness, global absence or exact external equivalent is asserted.
concepts.context_interpretation: R-12 makes the basis explicit for the assessment information; RK2-022 may identify the control baseline assumed. The documentary specification does not establish that the controls exist or are effective, and different bases cannot be silently pooled.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Dimension Assessment Result
concepts.authored_definition: A result for one assessment dimension, qualified by its method, scale, basis and relevant temporal context.
concepts.rationale: Retain DQV measurement as a pattern analogy. DQV concerns dataset quality; Riskium records a risk-dimension result with its own interpretation dependencies. DQV types and domain restrictions are not imported.
concepts.context_interpretation: R-48 identifies one dimension; R-14/R-15 and RX-016 retain optional scale, selected level and scale-version information. C-13/C-18 require compatible interpretation for comparison. The revised ArtifactVersion neighbor does not turn the result itself into a version or a measured real-world quality.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Assessment Method Specification
concepts.authored_definition: A versioned specification of procedures and rules used to produce and interpret assessment results.
concepts.rationale: Retain the reusable procedure/execution distinction from SOSA. A risk assessment method specification adds risk-specific interpretation rules; no SOSA restriction or full method equivalence is adopted.
concepts.context_interpretation: R-46/R-50 relate information and scores to a method; R-49 and RK2-018 describe permitted scales/dimensions. The specification retains documentary identity; a separately pinned ArtifactVersion identifies which issued content was used. A procedure description alone is not execution evidence.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Assessment Scale
concepts.authored_definition: A governed scale specification defining permissible values or ordered levels for a specified assessment dimension.
concepts.rationale: Retain NIST Table F-2 as an example of an interpreted severity scale. Its security-specific levels and numerical codes are not universal Riskium scales or probabilities and are not adopted as a mandatory scheme.
concepts.context_interpretation: RK2-019 declares one dimension, R-16 relates level resources to their scale, and version references qualify interpretation. Equal codes or labels across scales do not license ranking or arithmetic; qualitative values remain possible.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Risk Score Result
concepts.authored_definition: A numeric assessment output produced under a declared scoring method; it is not the risk itself or a universal definition of risk level.
concepts.rationale: Retain metric-qualified output as a DQV pattern analogy without equating dataset quality with risk. A recorded numeric output is neither the RiskCase nor an acceptability decision.
concepts.context_interpretation: R-50 requires a score method; R-18 permits zero or many component links for reported scores. C-21 separately requires declared components, a pinned method and adequate inputs for a computed score. C-18 preserves missing data as missing and does not certify a reported number as reproducible.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Assessment Scale Level
concepts.authored_definition: A managed vocabulary resource specifying a permissible value or category on an identified assessment scale version. It denotes a level; it is not a measured value occurrence or a bare lexical label.
concepts.rationale: Retain the SKOS distinction between an identified vocabulary resource and its lexical label. A level resource is not a value occurrence; this does not prohibit SKOS dual typing in general or adopt an OWL alignment.
concepts.context_interpretation: The VocabularyConcept ancestry preserves documentary identity; R-16 assigns one scale and R-15 selects a level for a result. C-13 also requires the selected level to match the scale version and dimension; a matching label alone is insufficient.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Assessment Dimension
concepts.authored_definition: A managed vocabulary resource specifying an assessment aspect, such as likelihood or consequence severity. The vocabulary item, the aspect denoted and its measured or judged value remain distinct.
concepts.rationale: Retain the DQV dimension/metric separation as a pattern analogy within its dataset-quality scope. Riskium uses a managed term for a risk-assessment aspect, distinct from the aspect denoted and the judged result.
concepts.context_interpretation: The path through ClassificationTerm/VocabularyConcept preserves scheme-qualified identity. R-48, RK2-018 and RK2-019 connect result, method and scale to the dimension. DQV metric requirements are not automatically added to the Riskium profile.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Epistemic Status Term
concepts.authored_definition: A controlled value indicating the evidential or epistemic character of a result, such as observed, estimated or projected. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
concepts.rationale: Retain SKOS vocabulary context for an observed, estimated or projected designation. SKOS does not establish that the designation is epistemically justified or that an estimate was observed.
concepts.context_interpretation: R-47 can qualify assessment information with a controlled status. Missing designation remains missing; the status resource, its text and the evidence supporting that status are separate. Retained incomplete/non-disjoint term groups are not newly approved as semantic partitions.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Uncertainty Statement
concepts.authored_definition: A managed statement of what is uncertain about a risk case, including assumptions and evidential limitations; it does not imply a numerical probability.
concepts.rationale: Retain the annotation body/target pattern for an uncertainty statement, without importing its serialization contract or treating the statement as a probability distribution.
concepts.context_interpretation: RX-004 concerns a continuing RiskCase; RK2-012/RK2-013 retain context and its use in assessment information. Revised RiskCase meaning was reviewed. Assumptions and evidential limitations may be qualitative; absence of a probability is not zero uncertainty.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Risk Evaluation Outcome
concepts.authored_definition: A recorded judgment of risk significance or acceptability based on identified assessment information and criteria versions. It is distinct from a numeric score and from the evaluation activity.
concepts.rationale: Retain the distinction between a criteria-based significance/acceptability judgment and a DQV metric result. This is a difference of intended role, not a global disjointness claim between external and local classes.
concepts.context_interpretation: RX-011 identifies the case, RX-012 requires assessment information and RX-013 pins a criteria ArtifactVersion. C-25 governs the versioned target. A numeric score alone does not establish acceptability or a treatment decision; revised case and version neighbors were reviewed.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported primary-passage comparison, current ancestry/neighbor/set-policy and selected assessment source-contract checks; not an instance or independent expert evaluation.

boundaries.static_scope: Selected source relations, identity suppliers and constraint statements; not new scoring, SQL, instance or ontology-engine executions.
boundaries.semantic_review: Independent semantic review remains #23; exact normative adoption remains #78.
boundaries.deployment_scope: Previews remain planning artifacts; complete component qualification and publication/readback remain separate.

batch_findings: All eleven authored definitions, direct edge records and inherited edges are unchanged. All inherit InformationArtifact identity; four concepts have changed association neighbors involving RiskCase and/or ArtifactVersion. Excluding the blanket artifact set preserves subtype edges without inventing exclusive or complete sibling partitions.

Ten labels are retained. AssessmentBasis changes its scoped-absence label to CONTRAST with generic PROV Entity, clarifying a difference in definitional scope rather than claiming no comparable work exists. The batch contains six ANALOGY, three RELATED and two CONTRAST decisions.

Assessment information, activity, dimensional result, method specification, scale/level, numeric score and criteria-based evaluation remain distinct. Optional received information is not declared task-ready merely because it has been recorded. Version targets follow the selected C-25 source statement; this packet does not newly execute dependency validation on real data.

C-18/C-21 preserve comparison dependencies, missingness and the reported/computed score distinction. A reported score may lack component links; a computed score has additional input/method obligations. A value alone establishes neither reproducibility nor acceptability. Full formula adequacy, all scale/unit compatibility and independent interpretation remain separate evaluation work.

The DQV comparisons are dataset-quality pattern analogies to a Working Group Note, not risk-specific standards conformance. NIST supplies security-specific documentary and scale examples. Neither DQV domain constraints nor NIST example codes are imported as universal risk rules.
context_guard_note: Documentary identity is separate from activity, risk identity and real-world values. Comparable interpretation requires the selected method/scale/dimension/basis/context/time or a justified transformation; missing input is not zero. A recorded score does not by itself establish acceptability, and a qualitative uncertainty statement need not contain probability.
source_access_note: Five primary HTML responses were directly retrieved and match their historical hashes. NIST direct HTTP attempts failed; the current B-9 glossary and F-2 scale were inspected through web PDF text and page images. Their selected passage fingerprints and exact locators are recorded; the historical full-PDF hash is retained separately and was not reverified. No source text is redistributed.
